meta.titulo: Catalogue assistant · Ámbar Furniture (fictional brand) · Ramiro Bales
meta.descripcion: A pre-sales assistant for e-commerce that answers only from the product page, cites every detail, says “not in the catalogue” instead of making things up and hands over to a person with a summary. Demo by Ramiro Bales with a fictional brand.
barra.tema: Switch between light and dark theme
cinta.texto: Demo by Ramiro Bales · Ámbar Furniture is a fictional brand created for this demo.
marca.aria: Ámbar Furniture, top of the demo
cabeza.titulo: A shop assistant that answers from the product page, or does not answer.
cabeza.bajada: Ask it the way a customer would. Every detail comes from a product page you can open; what is not there, it says so, and what is not its job, it hands to a person with a summary.
honesto.titulo: What this demo has and does not have
honesto.texto: This demo uses a local search engine and templates; in production the same design connects to a language model with retrieval (RAG) and the same rules: cite, do not make things up, hand over.
honesto.texto2: Everything runs in your browser: there is no server, nothing is stored and nothing is sent to anyone.
chat.sub: Answers from 12 product pages and 4 guides and policies
chat.bienvenida: Hi. I answer from Ámbar's product pages and show you where each detail comes from. If something is not there, I tell you; if you need someone on the team, I hand you over with a summary.
sug.2: How long does the table take to arrive?
sug.3: Will the Lúa armchair fit through a 70 cm door?
sug.4: If I order the Duna sofa in Moss velvet, when will it arrive?
sug.5: How do I get a stain out of velvet?
sug.6: What is the difference between the Duna and Bruma sofas?
entrada.label: Your question
entrada.ayuda: Dimensions, lead times, prices, care, warranty, delivery or comparisons. Press Enter to send.
traza.vacia1: Ask a question and you will see every step here: which words it understood, which catalogue passages it retrieved and with what score, which rule it applied, how it checked the figures and the fixed-schema output.
traza.pie: No server and no language model: the engine runs in your browser.
traza.pie.ms: Solved in {ms} ms in your browser · no server, no language model.
via.bm25: the top score, well ahead of the second
traza.bm25: BM25 (k1 1.2 · b 0.75) over {n} passages and {v} terms. ✓ = cited in the answer.
traza.bonos: Score = BM25 + 2 if the passage holds the detail asked for + 1.5 if it belongs to the chosen page.
traza.sinrecup: No passage shares terms with the question.
verif.ok: {c} figures in the answer: {e} appear in the cited passages or in your question{k}. It goes out.
verif.cero: The answer has no figures to check. It goes out.
verif.mal: Figures with no source: {f}. It does not go out; it is handed over.
persona.msg: I am handing you over to a person on the team. This is the summary they receive, so you do not have to repeat anything:
persona.cliente: I want to talk to a person
resumen.nota: In a real shop this goes into the team's inbox. In the demo it is not sent to anyone.
resumen.motivo.boton: The customer pressed “Talk to a person”.
resumen.aclarar: still has to choose which one
siguiente.posventa: This is after-sales: ask for the order number and photos, as the claims policy says, and reply on the same channel.
siguiente.sin: Answer what the catalogue does not have ({x}) and, if it keeps coming up, add it to the product page.
siguiente.venta: Pick up the sale of the {p}: they already have the product page details; offer to close the order or a visit.
siguiente.nada: Say hello and ask how you can help.
marca.titulo: Repeated questions answer themselves, and every answer can be audited.
marca.intro: Dimensions, lead times, care and warranty are the everyday questions in an online furniture shop, and the answers are already on the product pages. The assistant answers from those pages and leaves the team what needs judgement: claims, exceptions and custom sales. I do not give savings figures because this demo has no customers to measure; below is what I would measure.
gana1.p: “Will it fit through my door?”, “when does it arrive in this colour?”, “how do I clean it?”: answered from the product page right away, without waiting for someone on the team to be free.
gana2.p: The same question gets the same answer, because it comes from the product page and not from whoever is on shift. If a lead time changes in the catalogue, it changes in every answer at once.
gana3.p: Each answer keeps what was searched, which passages came up, which rule was applied and which page was cited. If a customer says “I was told something else”, you can see exactly what they were told and where it came from.
gana4.p: At night it answers what is in the catalogue, and what is not, it notes in a summary for the team, with what the customer asked and what they were already told. In the morning nobody starts from scratch.
gana4.b: See one that is not there
nohace.t: What it does not do, on purpose
nohace.1: It does not make up prices, lead times or dimensions: if they are not on the page, it says so.
nohace.2: It does not promise discounts or exceptions: it passes them to a person.
nohace.3: It does not resolve order claims: it writes the summary and hands over.
nohace.4: It does not guess which table you meant: if there are three, it asks which one.
conecta.titulo: Five pieces, and the last one is always a person.
conecta.intro: In a real shop the design is the same; what changes is what is inside each box. Under each one it says what stands in for it in this demo.
flujo1.p: The shop chat, WhatsApp, Instagram or email. They all reach the same assistant.
flujo2.p: Catalogue, policies and guides split into passages and indexed. When a product page changes, it is re-indexed automatically.
flujo3.p: It writes only from the retrieved passages and one of five rules: answer with a citation, clarify, “not there”, compare or hand over. It returns a fixed-schema output.
flujo3.d: hand-written templates; there is no model.
flujo4.p: Before sending, every figure in the answer has to appear in a cited passage. If one is missing, the answer does not go out and is handed over.
flujo4.d: the same check, on every answer.
flujo5.p: The team gets the summary in its inbox or ticketing system, decides the exceptions and replies. Their replies show what is missing from the catalogue.
flujo5.d: the summary is shown and can be copied; it is not sent.
medir.caption: What I would look at every week in production, and how it comes out in your conversation right now (it updates with every question).
medir.cita.p: If it drops, the assistant is answering things it cannot back up.
medir.deriva.p: How much work is left for the team. Too high: the catalogue is missing things; too low: it may be answering too much.
medir.noesta.p: The list of what people ask and the shop does not publish: it is the list of pages to complete.
medir.tiempo.p: In production it is measured end to end (with the model). Here only the local engine can be measured.

proceso.titulo: How I built it and how I test it.
brief.p: A pre-sales assistant for an online furniture shop that answers everyday questions from the product page. Acceptance criteria: every detail cited to its page, “not there” instead of making things up, a question back when the query is ambiguous, a hand-over to a person with a summary, a trail for every answer, and Spanish and English.
brief.como: I built it with AI-assisted development: I defined the brief, the rules, the catalogue and the test questions, and I checked every version by running the tests and looking at full-resolution screenshots.
dec1.i: In a shop, a made-up detail costs a return.
dec1.t: An answer goes out only if every figure appears in a cited passage.
dec1.no: I ruled out trusting that “the model cites properly”: the citation is checked, not assumed.
dec2.t: If more than one product fits, it asks which one before answering.
dec2.no: I ruled out picking the top score: it is almost always right and, when it is wrong, it gives the wrong lead time with total confidence.
dec3.i: Trust in the assistant is earned by showing how it decides.
dec3.t: A panel with every step, from the text of the question to the fixed-schema output.
dec3.no: I ruled out a “magic” chat with no explanation: nice for a demo, impossible to audit in a shop.
pruebas.p: Every change to the engine is tested against a fixed list of questions, in both languages, stating which rule and which page are expected. They run in your browser with the same engine as above. Passing them does not guarantee it understands any question: I wrote them, and when a new phrasing fails, it is added to the list.
pruebas.res: {ok} of {n} pass · median of {ms} ms per question
afuera1: There is no language model: the answers are templates. It understands the ways of asking I tested, not any sentence.
afuera2: The catalogue is fictional and small; with thousands of pages, the index would have to live on a server.
afuera3: The summary for the team is not sent anywhere: in production it would go to the inbox or the ticketing system.
afuera4: There is no history between visits and no customer data: every reload starts from scratch.
afuera5: I tested keyboard, focus and ARIA structure; I did not test with users or with real screen readers.
